problem.name: Normal hidden subgroup
problem.statement_latex: Given a finite group $G$ and an oracle constant and distinct on cosets of a normal subgroup $H\trianglelefteq G$, recover $H$. More generally, the procedure identifies the normal core of an arbitrary hidden subgroup.
problem.statement_text: Given a finite group $G$ and an oracle constant and distinct on cosets of a normal subgroup $H\trianglelefteq G$, recover $H$. More generally, the procedure identifies the normal core of an arbitrary hidden subgroup.

strength.description_latex: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.
strength.description_text: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.

evidence.description_latex: The cited results establish a classical lower bound separating the stated quantum resource bound in the specified model.
evidence.description_text: The cited results establish a classical lower bound separating the stated quantum resource bound in the specified model.

hardware.description_latex: The algorithm requires coherent input access and fault-tolerant execution of the stated procedure; its circuit and workspace requirements depend on that access implementation.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(\log|G|)$ Fourier samples by Hallgren--Russell--Ta-Shma; efficient gate complexity additionally requires an efficient quantum Fourier transform and efficient kernel-intersection processing for the chosen group.
quantum.headline_text: $O(\log|G|)$ Fourier samples by Hallgren–Russell–Ta-Shma; efficient gate complexity additionally requires an efficient quantum Fourier transform and efficient kernel-intersection processing for the chosen group.

classical.headline_latex: $O(|G|)$ queries by complete coset-label acquisition, while included abelian oracle families require $|G|^{\Omega(1)}$ randomized queries.
